We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to a phenyl ring which has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH (actually the amide attached to an aniline? Wait: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: that's an amide where the nitrogen is attached to phenyl with an NH substituent (an aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl that also has an NH (maybe an aniline). So the amide is N-aryl (anilide) with an ortho? Actually the SMILES: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl that has an NH substituent (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl bearing an NH (maybe para?). Not crucial.

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis: likely disconnections:

1. Amide formation (carboxylic acid + aniline) via coupling agent (forward: amide formation). So retrosynthetic step: break amide C-N, give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 1: target -> precursors: α,β-unsaturated acid (C= C-COOH attached to phenyl) and aniline.

2. The α,β-unsaturated acid could be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl with sulfonamide) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So break C=C double bond formation, break C-C bond (malonic acid) and C-O bond (aldehyde carbonyl). So step 2: break to give aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl-sulfonamide) and malonic acid (or maybe just malonic acid as simple reagent). So we can treat malonic acid as a simple building block (commercial). So step 2: target unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid.

3. The sulfonamide formation: the phenyl-sulfonyl chloride reacting with an aniline (p-toluidine). So break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the phenyl with sulfonamide). Wait the sulfonamide is attached to the phenyl ring (p-tolyl) as NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl ring (the sulfonyl group attached to the p-tolyl). Actually the sulfonamide is p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to the other phenyl (the one bearing the unsaturated amide). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl sulfonyl group and to the phenyl ring (the one with unsaturated chain). So the sulfonamide formation could be from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + the phenyl amine (the aromatic amine). So step 3: break S-N to give p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the aniline (the phenyl ring with the unsaturated chain). That aniline is the same as the aldehyde precursor? Actually the aldehyde precursor is the same phenyl ring (with sulfonamide nitrogen attached). Wait the aldehyde is the phenyl ring bearing the sulfonamide nitrogen? The aldehyde is the phenyl ring (the same as the sulfonamide-bearing phenyl) but with an aldehyde substituent (instead of the unsaturated chain). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (the same). So the sulfonamide formation step would involve the phenyl amine (the same phenyl ring) reacting with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride to give the sulfonamide. So the phenyl amine is the same as the aldehyde precursor (the aromatic amine). So we need to have that amine available before step 2 (Doebner). So retrosynthesis order: target -> break amide -> unsaturated acid + aniline (aniline is the phenyl with sulfonamide? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's a separate aniline (different phenyl). So there are two aniline moieties: one is the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to p-tolyl sulfonyl; the other is the aniline attached to the amide carbonyl. So step 1: break amide gives unsaturated acid (attached to phenyl-sulfonamide) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step 2: unsaturated acid derived from aldehyde (same phenyl-sulfonamide) via Doebner with malonic acid. So break to aldehyde (phenyl-sulfonamide) + malonic acid.

Step 3: phenyl-sulfonamide derived from sulfonyl chloride + aniline (the phenyl ring). So break to p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the phenyl amine (which is the same as aldehyde precursor? Wait the aldehyde precursor is phenyl amine with aldehyde substituent? Actually the aldehyde is on the phenyl ring (the same ring) but the amine is also on that ring (the sulfonamide nitrogen). The aldehyde is attached to the phenyl ring at para position relative to the sulfonamide? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2 attached to sulfonyl group: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the phenyl ring (c2ccc... ) has the sulfonamide nitrogen attached (via S). The aldehyde would be at the same position where the unsaturated chain attaches (the para position). So the aldehyde precursor is the same phenyl ring with sulfonamide attached and an aldehyde substituent. The sulfonamide formation step uses the same phenyl amine (the same ring) but with an amine group (NH2) that later becomes sulfonamide. However the aldehyde precursor still has the amine (NH2) to react with sulfonyl chloride. So step 3: phenyl amine (with aldehyde) + p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide (phenyl-sulfonamide) with aldehyde.

Thus the three steps are consistent.
